name: Rizon Card
summary: Rizon is a USD stablecoin wallet with a Visa Platinum card for spending USDC and USDT, aimed mainly at users in the US and Latin America. The virtual card costs US$10, USD card spending is free, and non-USD spending costs 1.7% + US$0.10, which the paid Emerald plan halves.

kyc.notes: You sign up with an email and then complete a short in-app KYC check. Rizon does not publish which documents it asks for.

pros: Virtual Visa Platinum card for US$10
Works with Apple Pay and Google Pay
Spend USDC and USDT wherever Visa is accepted
cons: 1.7% + US$0.10 fee on non-USD card spending
Mainly offered in the US and Latin America; no published country list
Fee figures differ between Rizon's own pages
ATM fees and limits are not clearly published

variants.name: Standard
variants.cardInfo: Virtual Visa Platinum · non-USD spend 1.7% + US$0.10

variants.name: Emerald plan
variants.cardInfo: From US$5.59/month · halves FX, trading and transaction fees

faq.question: How much does the Rizon Card cost?
faq.answer: The virtual card's standard price is US$10, though Rizon runs offers that lower it. Account maintenance is free and there is no monthly fee on the standard plan.

faq.question: What are the foreign-exchange fees on the Rizon Card?
faq.answer: USD card spending is free. Non-USD spending costs 1.7% + US$0.10 per transaction on the standard plan; the Emerald plan (from US$5.59/month) halves FX and transaction fees.

faq.question: What KYC does the Rizon Card require?
faq.answer: You sign up with an email and then complete a short in-app KYC check. Rizon does not publish the exact documents required.

faq.question: Which countries is Rizon available in?
faq.answer: Rizon does not publish a country list. Its terms say it focuses on the US and Latin America and does not actively offer its services in the EU. Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Russia, Belarus, Albania and Ukraine are among the restricted countries in its card terms.

faq.question: Which card network and wallets does the Rizon Card support?
faq.answer: It is a Visa Platinum card and works with Apple Pay and Google Pay.

fees.topup: Free account maintenance; USD card spend is free

availabilityNotes: Rizon does not publish a list of supported countries: its pages cite 122+ countries in one place and 178 in another, and its terms say it does not actively offer its services outside the US and Latin America, including in the EU. The restricted list here comes from Rizon's card terms (the card is issued through Rain) and is not exhaustive; it also covers Crimea, Donetsk and Luhansk. Check the country picker in the app before signing up.
howToGet: Download the Rizon app and sign up with your email.
Complete the short in-app KYC check.
Fund your USD balance with USDC or USDT.
Order the virtual Visa Platinum card (US$10 standard price; promotions may lower it).
Add the card to Apple Pay or Google Pay. Consider the Emerald plan only if you spend a lot in non-USD currencies.
